mechanism_narrative: A sustained 2% quarterly increase in real GDP growth (GDPC1) over the preceding year signals a robust expansion in aggregate demand, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings prospects improve.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth exceeds 3% quarterly for 3 consecutive quarters but S&P 500 20d returns remain negative in > 60% of those periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 2% monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over the prior 3 months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate profit margins compress.
failure_condition: If INDPRO declines by > 3% monthly for 3 months but S&P 500 20d returns are positive in > 60% of those periods, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5% monthly increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior 3 months signals a tightening monetary cycle, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as discount rates rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises by > 1% monthly for 3 months but S&P 500 20d returns are positive in > 60% of those periods, the hypothesis is falsified.
